chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Abhari narrated to me. He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari al-Ghilabi al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Shu'ayb ibn Waqid narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Yazid narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: Prohibited

the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from eating whilst in a state of sexual impurity. He said: 'It bequeaths poverty.' He prohibited cutting nails with teeth, using the toothstick in the bathroom, and blowing the nose in the mosques. He prohibited eating from the leftovers of mice. He said: 'Do not go to the mosque without praying at least two units.' He prohibited urination under a fruit tree and at the side of a road. He prohibited eating with the left hand and eating while lying down.

He prohibited plastering graveyards and praying in them. He said: 'When one of you bathes in an expanse of earth, be mindful of your private parts. None of you should drink water from the handle of a vessel, for it is a gathering place for dirt.' He prohibited urinating in still water, for it causes a loss in intellect. He prohibited walking with one sandal and putting on sandals while standing. He prohibited urinating while the private faces the Sun or Moon. He said: 'When you defecate, avoid the qibla.' He prohibited screaming during calamities. He prohibited wailing and listening to it.

He prohibited women from following funeral processions. He prohibited erasing anything from the Book of Allah with saliva or writing in it. He prohibited lying purposely about dreams. He said: 'Allah will order him to tie a knot in a grain of barley and he will not be able.' He prohibited creating images. He said: 'Whoever creates an image, Allah will order him to blow life into it on the Day of Resurrection and he will not be able.' He prohibited burning a living animal. He prohibited insulting the rooster. He said: 'It calls to prayer.'

He prohibited interfering in a deal of his Muslim brother. He prohibited speaking too much during intercourse. He said: 'It causes muteness in the child.' He said: 'Do not sleep while garbage is in your house. Take it out during the day, for it is a sitting place for Satan.' He said: 'Do not sleep while the residue of meat is on your hand, for you will be afflicted with mild insanity from Satan.' He prohibited cleaning oneself with dung. He prohibited women from leaving their house without husband's permission. He prohibited a woman from adorning herself for other than her husband. He prohibited women from speaking more than five unnecessary words to non-relatives. He prohibited women from seeing each other without a robe. He prohibited women from discussing confidential matters about their husbands. He prohibited intercourse facing the qibla or on a paved road. He prohibited men from saying: 'Marry me to your sister so I may marry you to mine.'

He prohibited visiting fortune-tellers. He said: 'Whoever visits and believes him has dissociated from what Allah revealed to Muhammad.' He prohibited playing with dice, chess, drums, tambourines, and ouds. He prohibited backbiting and listening to it. He prohibited gossiping and listening to it. He said: 'A gossiper will not enter Paradise.' He prohibited responding to invitations from the depraved. He prohibited false oaths. He said: 'They lead to loss of houses.' He said: 'Whoever swears a false oath to take a Muslim's wealth will meet Allah angry, unless he repents.' He prohibited sitting at tables where wine is drunk. He prohibited men from bringing their women to bathhouses. He said: 'Enter bathhouses only with an izar.' He prohibited conversations calling to other than Allah. He prohibited slapping the face. He prohibited drinking from gold or silver vessels. He prohibited men from wearing silk, but for women there is no problem.

He prohibited selling fruits before they bloom. He prohibited selling dates before they ripen and grapes and the like. He prohibited selling dice and chess. He said: 'Whoever does that is like one who ate pork.' He prohibited selling wine, buying wine, and providing wine. He (as) said: 'May Allah curse wine, its presser, its planter, its drinker, its provider, its seller, its buyer, the consumer of its wealth, its carrier, and the one it is carried to.' He (as) said: 'Whoever drinks it, prayers are not accepted for forty days. If he dies with it in his stomach, Allah will make him drink his own pus.' He prohibited consuming usury, bearing false witness, and issuing usury. He (as) said: 'Allah curses the consumer of usury, its dealer, its issuer, and its witness.' He prohibited lending on condition of sale. He prohibited two sales in one. He prohibited selling what you do not have. He prohibited selling what cannot be guaranteed.

He prohibited shaking hands with the dhimmi. He prohibited reciting poetry or announcing lost items in the mosque. He prohibited unsheathing swords in the mosque. He prohibited striking the faces of animals. He prohibited men from looking at the privates of their Muslim brethren. He said: 'Whoever stares, seventy thousand angels curse him.' He prohibited women from looking at privates of women. He prohibited blowing into food, drink, or the place of prostration. He prohibited praying in graveyards, roads, roundabouts, valleys, camel stalls, and atop the Ka'ba. He prohibited killing bees. He prohibited branding faces of animals. He prohibited swearing on other than Allah. He prohibited swearing on a chapter from the Book of Allah. He prohibited saying: 'No, by your life.' He prohibited sitting in the mosque in a state of impurity. He prohibited nudity day and night. He prohibited cupping on Wednesdays and Fridays. He prohibited speaking while the imam delivers the Friday sermon. He prohibited wearing brass or iron rings. He prohibited etching animals on rings.

He prohibited praying at three times: sunrise, sunset, and zenith. He prohibited fasting on six days: Fitr, day of doubt, sacrifice, and the days of tashriq. He prohibited sipping water like animals. He said: 'Drink with your hands, they are the best utensils.' He prohibited spitting in wells. He prohibited hiring a worker before knowing the wage. He prohibited ignoring a person for more than three days. He prohibited selling gold and silver at one price. He prohibited selling gold for gold except equal weight. He prohibited overpraising. He said: 'Throw dust in the faces of those who overpraise.'

He (s) said: 'Whoever supports an oppressor, when the Angel of Death comes, it will say: I give you tidings of Allah's curse and the Fire.' He said: 'Whoever praises a tyrannical leader will follow him to the Fire.' He (s) said: 'Allah says: Do not incline to the oppressors or the Fire will touch you.' [11:113] He (s) said: 'Whoever guides a tyrant to injustice will be the companion of Haman in Hell. Whoever builds for show will carry it from the seventh earth as fire on the Day of Resurrection.' He (s) said: 'Whoever oppresses a worker's wage, Allah invalidates his deeds. Whoever usurps a hand-span of his neighbor's land, Allah will make it a collar from the seventh earth.' Whoever learns the Quran then deliberately forgets it will meet Allah chained, with a snake for every verse. He (s) said: 'Whoever recites the Quran then drinks something forbidden or prefers worldly love, Allah's wrath is upon him.' If he dies without repenting, the Quran will contest him on the Day of Resurrection.

Whoever commits adultery with any woman, free or bond, and dies insistent, Allah opens three hundred gates to his grave from which snakes and scorpions of the Fire emerge. He burns until Resurrection. When resurrected, people seek refuge from his stench. Allah forbade the forbidden and set the limits. He prohibited looking into a neighbor's house. He said: 'Whoever looks at his brother's private parts intentionally, Allah includes him among the hypocrites. He will be exposed before leaving this world.' He (s) said: 'Whoever is not pleased with his sustenance and does not exercise patience, his good deeds will not be raised.' He prohibited strutting. He said: 'Whoever wears a robe and struts, Allah takes him to Hell's edge, following Qarun who was the first to strut.'

Whoever struts has challenged Allah in His might. He (s) said: 'Whoever oppresses a woman of her dowry is an adulterer before Allah.' On the Day of Resurrection Allah will say: 'My servant! I married you to My maidservant upon My covenant but you did not fulfill it.' [17:34] He prohibited concealing testimony. 'Whoever conceals it, Allah feeds his flesh.' That is: 'Do not conceal the testimony.' [2:283] He said: 'Whoever harms his neighbor, Paradise's fragrance is forbidden. Gabriel kept advising me about neighbors until I thought he would make them inherit. He kept advising about slaves until I thought they would be freed. He kept advising about the toothstick until I thought it would become obligatory. He kept advising about night prayer until I thought the best of my Nation would not sleep.'

Whoever belittles a poor Muslim, Allah belittles him on the Day of Resurrection, unless he repents. He (s) said: 'Whoever honors a poor Muslim meets Allah pleased.' He (s) said: 'Whoever is presented with temptation and avoids it out of fear of Allah, He forbids the Fire from him and safeguards him from the Great Dismay. For he who fears standing before his Lord is two gardens.' [55:46] Whoever chooses this world over the Hereafter meets Allah without a good deed. Whoever fills his eye with forbidden things, Allah fills his eye with fire. Whoever shakes hands with a forbidden woman comes with Allah's anger. Whoever cheats a Muslim is not of us and will be with the Jews. He prohibited depriving anyone of kindness. He said: 'Whoever deprives his neighbor of kindness, Allah deprives him of goodness.'

He (s) said: 'When a woman harms her husband with her tongue, Allah does not accept her deeds until she pleases him, even if she fasts, prays, frees slaves, and fights in Allah's cause. She will be first to the Fire. Same for the man if oppressive.' Whoever strikes a Muslim's cheek, Allah scatters his bones on Resurrection and he is chained until Hell, unless he repents. Whoever sleeps while cheating his Muslim brother has slept upon Allah's anger. He prohibited backbiting. He said: 'Whoever backbites a Muslim invalidates his fasting and cancels his ablution. He comes on Resurrection smelling like a corpse.' He (s) said: 'Whoever forbears while capable, Allah gives martyr's reward.'

Whoever refutes backbiting of his brother in a gathering, Allah repels seventy gates of harm. If he does not refute while able, he has the sin of seventy backbitings. He prohibited betrayal. 'Whoever betrays a trust and dies will have died on other than my creed.' He said: 'Whoever bears false witness, his tongue is hung with hypocrites in the lowest Fire.' Whoever hires a betrayer knowingly is like the betrayer. Whoever withholds a Muslim brother's right, Allah forbids sustenance's blessing. Whoever hears an indecency and spreads it is like the one who did it. Whoever can give a loan but refuses, Paradise's fragrance is forbidden. Whoever exercises patience over a difficult spouse, Allah gives rewards of the thankful. If a woman is not compassionate and burdens her spouse beyond capacity, her good deeds are not accepted. Whoever honors his Muslim brother honors Allah. He prohibited leading prayer without permission.

He said: 'Whoever leads prayer with permission and they are pleased, and beautifies his prayer, he has their reward without decreasing theirs. Whoever leads but does not perfect his prayer, it is rejected and does not rise above his position, like an oppressive leader.' He said: 'Whoever walks to a relative to connect ties, Allah gives reward of one hundred martyrs, forty thousand good deeds per step, forty thousand sins erased, raised in rank, as if he worshiped one hundred years.' Whoever fulfills a blind person's need, Allah dissociates him from hypocrisy and the Fire, fulfills seventy needs. Whoever is ill for a day and night without complaining, Allah raises him with Ibrahim the Friend. Whoever goes for an ill person's need comes out sinless as the day his mother bore him. A man asked about family members being ill. He said: Yes. Whoever relieves a believer of a burden, Allah relieves seventy-two burdens of the Hereafter.

Whoever invalidates a rightful person's right will have ten sins each day. Whoever whips in front of a tyrant, Allah makes that whip a fire serpent seventy cubits long. Whoever does a good deed then boasts, Allah invalidates his deeds. He (s) said: 'Allah says: Paradise is forbidden for the wealthy miser, the backbiter, and the gossiper.' Whoever gives charity, each coin is like Mount Uhud of Paradise's blessings. Whoever brings charity to the needy has the owner's reward. Whoever prays over the dead, seventy thousand angels pray over him. Whoever attends burial has a carat per step like Mount Uhud. Whoever sheds tears in humility before Allah has a palace in Paradise. Whoever goes to the mosque for congregation has seventy thousand good deeds per step. If he dies doing that, Allah assigns seventy thousand angels to visit him in his grave.

Whoever gives the call to prayer seeking Allah's face, Allah grants reward of forty thousand martyrs and forty thousand saints, and forty thousand sinners enter Paradise through his intercession. When the mu'adhin says 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' ninety thousand angels bless him. When he says 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' forty thousand angels record his deeds. Whoever secures the first row and first takbir without harming a Muslim gets the mu'adhin's reward. Whoever aligns with a fortune-teller, Allah imprisons him at Hell's edge for a thousand years per day. If he was oppressive, he falls into Hell. He (s) said: 'Do not underestimate evil no matter how small, and do not overestimate goodness. There is nothing too big for repentance, nothing too small for persistence.'

Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Ghilabi said: I asked Shu'ayb al-Muzni about the length of this report. He said to me: O Abu Abdillah! I asked al-Husayn ibn Zayd about the length of this hadith, and he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to me that he gathered this hadith from a book that was the dictations of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الجنابة: State of ritual impurity (janaba) requiring ghusl before worship
key_terms.الربا: Usury or interest, prohibited in Islamic law
key_terms.الغيبة: Backbiting - speaking ill of someone in their absence
key_terms.القبلة: The direction of prayer (qibla) toward the Ka'ba in Mecca
key_terms.المحاقلة: Selling fresh dates for dry dates, a prohibited type of barter
key_terms.النميمة: Tale-bearing and gossip that causes discord between people
key_terms.النياحة: Wailing loudly in lamentation, prohibited in Islam

ai.seo_question: What are the comprehensive prohibitions of Prophet Muhammad in Islam?
ai.summary: This extraordinarily long hadith is a comprehensive compilation of the Prophet Muhammad's (s) prohibitions (nawaahi) and exhortations, transmitted through the chain of Shia Imams from Imam Ali (as). It was originally recorded as a single document from the dictations of the Prophet (s) in the handwriting of Imam Ali (as). The hadith covers an extensive range of topics including personal hygiene, dietary rules, gender conduct, commercial transactions, criminal punishments, worship regulations, social obligations, and eschatological warnings. It served as a practical legal and ethical manual for the early Muslim community, codifying scores of rulings into a single authoritative compilation. The original audience would have understood this as a codex of Prophetic law touching nearly every aspect of daily life.
